data.title: Oracle's Q1 proves potential of IaaS strategy as cloud infra surges 121%: analysts
data.description:
Oracle's (ORCL) first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings results proved the potential of its infrastructure as a service strategy as cloud infrastructure revenue surged 121% year over year to $7.4B.

Shares initially popped up about 7% during post-market trading on Thursday. However, by noon trading on Friday, shares had increased less than 1%. Despite the lukewarm next-day reaction in the market, analysts across the board were positive on the results.

J.P. Morgan reiterated its Outperform rating and $200 price target.

"The company delivered to expectations with total revenue growth of +30% y/y, tracking above the guide on triple-digit growth in Cloud Infrastructure, and RPO building a further $26B sequentially," said J.P. Morgan analyst Samik Chatterjee in a Friday investor note.

"The strength was evident across multiple drivers: 1) Capacity delivery of 850 MW in the quarter, nearly three times what was delivered in all of F4Q26 and none of it from the flagship sites that have attracted investor scrutiny, which in our view demonstrates the diversification of the build-out and mitigates risk to the medium-term outlook from any single site delay; 2) More than $30B of new AI contracts, primarily booked on prepay or bring-your-own-hardware (BYOH) structures; and 3) Operating leverage and discipline that helped hold PF operating margin flat at ~42% despite the expected step-down in gross margin, reinforcing our view that operating margin, rather than gross margin, is the appropriate lens as infrastructure becomes a larger share of the mix," he added.

Meanwhile, Jefferies reiterated its Buy rating and $290 price target, highlighting Oracle's significant backlog.

"Backlog was $664B (46% y/y growth), up 4% q/q ($26B q/q) vs. 15% in F4Q26 and 6% q/q in F3Q26," said Jefferies analyst Brent Thill in a note. "On a y/y basis, backlog decelerated vs. 363% y/y growth in F4Q. The backlog growth was driven by >$30B of additional AI cloud contracts booked in F1Q. Mgmt indicated that based on the structuring of those new contracts, there is no incremental impact on its plans to raise capital."

Similarly, Citi reiterated its Buy rating and hefty $330 price target.

"Oracle delivered more than 300,000 GPUs during the quarter while adding 850MW of datacenter capacity and older GPUs seeing 20% premium on renewed and resold contracts," Citi analysts said in a note. Roughly half of RPO is expected to flow into revenue over the next 36 months, with RPO conversion to revenue expected to accelerate. Multicloud DB cloud grew 353% y/y, and multicloud customers grew 180% y/y, with multicloud DB regions reaching 70. They also completed their $20B at-the-market equity issuance in Q1."

data.title: Vicor soars 11% on bullish demand sentiment
data.description:
Shares of Vicor Corporation (VICR), a designer and manufacturer of modular power components, rallied just over 10% on Friday. The news came after the company announced plans to acquire two manufacturing sites in New Hampshire to support the construction of ChiP Fab-2 and Fab-3. This played into bullish sentiment about the company's demand prospects.

The stock climbed $19.06 to trade at $197.11 as of 11:45 a.m. ET, rebounding from a stretch of weakness that had weighed on the shares over the prior sessions.

data.title: QatarEnergy in talks with Venture Global, others for U.S. LNG deals - Reuters
data.description:
QatarEnergy is negotiating with several producers including Venture Global (VG), Cheniere Energy (LNG), and Woodside Energy (WDS) to secure long-term U.S. liquefied natural gas contracts through 2031 to replace capacity knocked out by Iranian attacks that will ​take years to repair, Reuters reported Friday.

The discussions would mark a shift from QatarEnergy's purchases ​of dozens of U.S. spot LNG cargoes to help meet commitments to some of its ⁠Asian clients, suggesting it is now seeking longer-term solutions to cover the shortfall.

The contract reportedly talks are part of Qatar's attempts to replace lost volumes from its Ras Laffan facility after two of its 14 LNG trains and a gas-to-liquids facility were damaged by Iranian ​strikes in March.

After halting production, QatarEnergy has renewed force majeure notices monthly, most recently extended to November, with further extensions possible as the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

Qatar's pursuit of long-term LNG volumes from other producers to help fulfill customer contracts "indicates that Qatar now sees ​risk to their ability to ​export LNG for several ⁠years," MST Marquee head of energy research Saul Kavonic told Reuters.

data.title: Moderna climbs 8% as volatile trading continues
data.description:
Moderna (MRNA) shares jumped just over 8% on Friday, continuing a volatile stretch for the biotechnology company following a landmark Phase 3 cancer trial result announced in August. As of 11:45am ET, shares were trading at $148.13, up $11.51 from the previous close.

The stock has surged more than 128% over the past month after Moderna and Merck announced that intismeran autogene, their individualized mRNA cancer therapy developed in combination with Keytruda, met its primary endpoint in the Phase 3 INTerpath-001 melanoma trial. Today's session extended a partial recovery from a stretch of losses in the days prior.

data.title: Flex advances 8% amid tech sector strength
data.description:
Shares of Flex Ltd. (FLEX), a global manufacturing and supply-chain company, rallied nearly 8% on Friday, recovering ground after the stock dropped more than 4% the previous session. The advance came amid broader market strength, with the technology sector among the leading gainers on the day.

Last week, Flex announced an agreement to acquire EPC Power for $4.4 billion, a transaction that adds power-conversion capabilities targeted at AI data centers and grid applications. The deal was announced on September 3 and is expected to become part of Flex's Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment, which the company plans to separate into an independent publicly traded company in the first calendar quarter of 2027.

data.title: IG Metall moves to reopen talks with Volkswagen
data.description:
Germany’s IG Metall union is pushing Volkswagen (VWAGY) to reaffirm its commitment to a labor agreement reached in 2024, adding pressure on management as the carmaker pursues a sweeping restructuring.

Union members voted Friday to activate a provision in the agreement that brings management and labor back to the negotiating table. IG Metall says workers need clarity over whether commitments made under the deal will remain intact as Volkswagen (VWAGY) considers deeper job and production cuts.

The dispute has intensified around plans that could eventually eliminate about 100,000 positions and significantly reduce manufacturing capacity. Volkswagen (VWAGY) is also weighing plant closures as it confronts competition from Chinese automakers, high production costs,costs and increased tariff expenses.

Works council chief Daniela Cavallo rejected the idea that German costs alone were responsible for the company’s difficulties. She called for stronger European measures to protect manufacturers from competitors benefiting from state support in China.

Volkswagen (VWAGY) said it welcomed the talks, arguing that discussions would help implement measures agreed in 2024 while addressing new pressures facing the automotive industry.

The earlier agreement followed large-scale walkouts and included about 35,000 job cuts and wage concessions. In exchange, workers secured commitments on investment and the future of some facilities.

IG Metall cannot call strikes under existing labor agreements until the end of the year, media sources reported.

data.title: J.P. Morgan initiates Getty Images, Yelp, and Angi Inc. with Underweight rating
data.description:
J.P. Morgan analyst Bryan Smilek initiated coverage of Getty Images (GETY), Yelp (YELP), and Angi Inc. (ANGI) with an Underweight rating attributed to factors that include limited visibility, macro dynamics, and uncertainties surrounding a strategic pivot to an AI-native platform.

  • Getty Images (GETY): Underweight: Smilek is encouraged by Getty Images’ focus on optimizing its balance sheet and its strong assets. But Smilek’s Underweight rating stems from Getty Images’ $2.1B in outstanding debt and revenue loss in Q2.
  • “Overall, we’re encouraged by GETY’s focus on balance sheet optimization, and we believe the company maintains strong assets across its content, customer base, leading scale, and established brand. However, visibility is limited, and we look for strategic updates across growth initiatives and balance sheet optimization,” Smilek writes in his note.
  • Getty Images’ (GETY) shares are down as much as 6% on Friday.

 

  • Yelp: Underweight, $19 price target:  Yelp maintains a "significant" monetization opportunity, Smilek writes, but the company faces competitive pressures from food ordering and delivery providers and macro headwinds that are weighing on local businesses.
  • “Overall, we’re positive on YELP’s AI transformation, product-led strategy, scaling data licensing business, and continued cost discipline. However, visibility remains limited, and macro dynamics remain unfavorable.”
  • Yelp (YELP) shares are fractionally higher on Friday. 

 

  • Angi Inc. (ANGI): Underweight: Smilek expects Angi (ANGI) to make progress towards achieving $5B annual revenue but notes Q2 revenue was down 11% driven by network declines and lower spending across select paid marketing channels as well as softer macro trends that impacted Pro spending.
  • “However, our Underweight rating reflects recent growth challenges amid an unfavorable macro backdrop and limited visibility into Angi’s strategic pivot to an AI-native platform.”  
  • Angi (ANGI) shares are down more than 1%.

data.title: Neuronetics a new buy at B Riley on interventional psychiatry platform
data.description:
• B Riley has initiated Neuronetics (STIM) at buy, saying that the company is set to benefit from a psychedelic-driven shift in interventional psychiatry.
  • The investment bank has a $5 price target (~66% upside based on Sept. 10 close). 
  • While Neuronetics has traditionally focused on transcranial magnetic stimulation ("TMS") treatment for depression, its late-2024 acquisition of Greenbrook TMS "transformed Neuronetics from a transcranial magnetic stimulation capital equipment vendor into a vertically integrated interventional psychiatry platform."
  • Analyst Madison El-Saadi said that the deal added Greenbrook's 93-center clinic network that provides both TMS and treatment with Johnson & Johnson's (JNJ) Spravato (esketamine), a drug related to ketamine, which has hallucinogenic effects. Spravato's US sales surpassed a $2B run rate in Q1.
  • He noted that the company has replaced executives this year with a new CEO, CFO, and chief legal officer, adding that revenue is increasing and Q2 was its first adjusted EBITDA-positive quarter.
  • "STIM’s valuation understates Greenbrook’s growth profile, in our opinion, with the stock trading at a bottom-quartile multiple despite its services segment growing above peer averages," El-Saadi wrote.

data.title: US regulators look to create framework for risks associated with banks' third-party ties
data.description:
U.S. regulators are looking to create a framework to assist financial institutions with managing risks associated with third-party relationships.

In a joint statement, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the Federal Reserve Board, the National Credit Union Administration, and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency requested public comments on its proposed guidance.

"Banking organizations routinely rely on third parties for a range of products, services, and other activities," said the joint statement. "The agencies have long acknowledged both the benefits associated with third-party relationships and the potential that these relationships may present or, in some cases, heighten certain risks."

"The proposed guidance would address these concerns by emphasizing risk identification and assessment as the foundation of a risk-based approach. This would enable banking organizations and examiners to focus on material financial risks and violations of laws and regulations rather than ineffective and counterproductive check-the-box exercises," said the statement.

"The proposed guidance would also encourage responsible innovation, consistent with Executive Order 14405, by emphasizing a risk-based and tailored approach to third-party risk management and removing broad-based and overly prescriptive language from the 2023 Guidance that may unduly impede fintechs from entering partnerships with banking organizations," said the guidance.

The comments are due 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.

The non-binding principles-based approach intends to assist banks and credit unions to better align and tailor their third-party risk management practices to the risks of individual third-party relationships.

Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) rose almost 9% on Friday, pushing the stock above its 52-week high as the analog semiconductor maker continued a strong multi-session run.
